s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Numerous eosinophils were present on biopsy
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Numerous eosinophils on biopsy and perivascular inflammation

shortlist.label: Immunotherapy-associated dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, which can cause dermatitis

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous annular plaques on skin, matching clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular inflammation and presence of eosinophils on biopsy

shortlist.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving pembrolizumab, which can cause skin rash as a side effect

raw.rationale: The patient's rash started after initiation of immunotherapy with pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, and the biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils are consistent with an immune-mediated reaction.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: While eosinophils are present, the clinical presentation and timing in relation to immunotherapy initiation better support an immunotherapy-associated reaction.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: The condition is characterized by annular lesions, but it doesn't fully explain the temporal relationship with immunotherapy or the specific inflammatory findings on biopsy.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: This condition involves inflammation of the blood vessel walls, which is not the primary finding in this case, where perivascular and interstitial inflammation is noted without specific mention of vasculitis.

rejected.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
rejected.why: This option is too narrow, as the patient is also receiving ipilimumab, and the term 'immunotherapy-associated dermatitis' encompasses reactions to both or either of these medications.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: Already considered and rejected due to the broader context of immunotherapy initiation and the specific biopsy findings
